title: Risk-On Liquidity Expansion: Carry, Beta, and the Complacency Failure Mode
content: In a risk-on liquidity expansion regime, central bank easing or abundant global dollar liquidity compresses credit spreads toward historical lows and suppresses realized volatility, rewarding carry and high-beta positioning as the dominant return sources. As the regime matures, the feedback loop tightens: low vol encourages systematic de-hedging, crowded carry trades amplify beta extension, and tight spreads reduce compensation for tail risk, collectively building a fragility stack that is invisible in contemporaneous metrics. The complacency failure mode triggers when an exogenous shock — policy pivot, credit event, or funding-currency unwind — forces rapid deleveraging; because the unwind is endogenous to position size, the reversal is convex and self-reinforcing rather than gradual. Credit spreads, particularly high-yield, are historically reliable early-warning indicators: a decisive widening beyond regime anchors signals that liquidity is repricing before equity volatility fully registers. Macro strategies should monitor the spread between implied and realized vol, carry-trade positioning crowding, and speculative-grade default rates as leading indicators of regime exhaustion.
lesson: Low vol and tight credit are not confirmation of safety — they are the surface expression of accumulated complacency; the regime is most dangerous precisely when it feels most comfortable, because position crowding and de-hedging make the reversal convex and fast.
